name: Ittai
overview: Ittai was a male warrior known as the Gittite, distinguished as the seventeenth member of "the thirty," a group of David's elite men. His tribal affiliation is not recorded in Scripture, but his loyalty to David during significant events highlights his importance. The biblical record provides no additional personal notes about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Ittai, also spelled Ithai, means "with me," indicating a possible expression of loyalty or companionship. This proper name is not given by God but appears in the biblical text, emphasizing his identity as a trusted follower of David.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Ittai was the son of Ribai. Beyond this paternal relationship, the Bible does not provide further details about his family or lineage apart from his designation as the Gittite.
scriptureSignificance: Ittai's significance lies in his role as a devoted warrior within David's elite group, "the thirty," underscoring his valor and commitment during David's reign. His identification as the Gittite suggests a non-Israelite origin, yet his allegiance to David exemplifies faithfulness beyond tribal boundaries. Through his service, Ittai contributes to the narrative of God's providential preservation of David's kingship.
